claims.text: Adding a sintering aid by a liquid-phase method can lower the preparation temperature required for ZrB2 ceramic to below 2300 °C.
Adding a sintering aid by a liquid-phase method can reduce holes in ZrB2 ceramic.
Reducing holes through sintering-aid addition can reduce eventual component failure during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
The sintering aid enhances densification of ZrB2 ceramic.
Enhanced densification reduces the number of holes in the material.
Enhanced densification improves the overall strength of the material.
Sintering-aid-modified ZrB2 will have better structural integrity than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
Sintering-aid-modified ZrB2 will exhibit less component failure than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
The proposed preparation boundary is a temperature below 2300 °C.
The proposed service boundary includes prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
The hypothesis is falsified if modified samples fail to show at least a 20% improvement in structural integrity and a 30% reduction in component failure relative to conventional samples.
